title: wbs solver wire contract, version 1
$comment: THE single normative definition of the solver request and response (design.md 'Solver wire contract — one versioned schema, four consumers', Sol r6 Critical 1). Prose in tasks.md, design.md and spec.md is descriptive only; where they disagree with this file, this file wins and the prose is the bug. Four consumers read it: the Bun request builder and parseSolverResponse in libs/contracts/solver/src/, the wbs-solver Python entrypoint validating against the copy installed beside it with the pinned jsonschema dependency, and the shared golden corpus under libs/contracts/solver/fixtures/ that both suites run. The root asserts `not: {}` on purpose: neither message validates against the document itself, so a consumer that forgets to $ref a branch fails loudly instead of accepting anything. Validate #/$defs/request or #/$defs/response.

units.$comment: UNITS USED BY THIS FILE. `unit` = one quantised solver time unit; quantum units make one workday, and SOLVER_QUANTUM = 48 (design.md 'Time quantisation'). notBeforeUnits, deadlineUnits, durationUnits, horizonUnits, every baselineOffsets/fastHint/offsets value and every objective value/stageValue/bound are in units. budgetMs is in milliseconds of wall clock. width is in people. A pool size is in slots. stageBudgetSplit entries are dimensionless fractions of budgetMs.

wireVersion.$comment: Required literal on every message in both directions. Encoded as the integer 1 rather than a string: this is a schema generation, not a name, and a version bump ships a new file solver-wire.v2.json beside this one rather than widening this const. RECORDED CHOICE — the artifacts require `wireVersion` to be 'a required literal' and fix nothing else about it.

safeInteger.$comment: Non-negative and bounded by Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER inclusive. This is the Bun/JSON exactness bound, deliberately tighter than CP-SAT's signed 64-bit range, so Bun can recompute a term and compare a one-unit difference exactly (design.md 'Objective mathematics', tasks.md 2.1). Every integer objective field in both directions carries it.

sliceKey.$comment: sliceKey(workItemId, stepId) verbatim (libs/domain/src/schedule.ts:105): the two ids joined by a literal U+0000, with a null stepId rendered as the empty string. NO `pattern` and NO `propertyNames` constraint beyond this: every real key CONTAINS a U+0000, so any printable-character pattern would reject every valid request. Legal JSON, and it survives JSON.stringify and json.loads unchanged. The golden corpus carries such a key verbatim rather than a sanitised stand-in, and a request log is not the place this is discovered.

offsetMap.$comment: A slice-keyed map of integer unit offsets from day zero. MAP, not an array of pairs, because the response `offsets` is normatively 'that offsets map' (spec.md, 'The solver response SHALL carry only ...'), MOVEMENT is written as the subscript access `Σ |start(s) − baselineOffsets[s]|` (tasks.md 4.x/objective mathematics), and the three fields that use this shape — baselineOffsets, fastHint and offsets — are one domain in one unit and must not differ in form. WHAT THIS SHAPE CANNOT ENFORCE, and what therefore has to be a builder/consumer check: (1) a JSON object with a duplicate key is silently deduped by both JSON.parse and json.loads, so no schema anywhere can reject one — both consumers check the parsed key count against the raw member count; (2) key-set equality with slices[].key; (3) every value <= horizonUnits. See #/$defs/request's own $comment for the full list of cross-field invariants.

edge.$comment: An OBJECT of two slice keys, mirroring the domain's own DependencyEdge = { predecessorId, successorId } (schedule.ts:7) rather than a positional pair, because the endpoints are asymmetric and a 2-array hides which is which at every call site. SLICE-keyed, not work-item-keyed: the solver receives no work item ids and no tree. The conversion from expandToLeaves' DependencyEdge[] (schedule.ts:337) is real work rather than a rename, because one leaf holds many slices, and the two endpoints are chosen by DIFFERENT rules — predecessor = reachedSliceOf(reach, slices) (schedule.ts:1676: slices.length - 1 under whole-item; under anchor-slice the first slice with days !== null, falling back to the last), successor = the first slice plain under EITHER reach (schedule.ts:1718). That asymmetry is deliberate and no fixture with one slice per item can reveal it. Edges arrive already leaf-expanded with reach applied and already carrying the intra-item step-order edges, so Python never sees the tree, parentId or dep_reach.

workItemKey.$comment: Opaque work-item identity shared by every slice of one work item. Carried separately so Bun and Python can prove the bidirectional workItemIsMilestone fact by grouping slices without parsing sliceKey's deliberately opaque representation.

durationUnits.$comment: units. ceil(duration(s) × quantum) with duration(s) computed by Fast's exact rule: ASSUMED_SLICE_WORKDAYS for a null days WITHOUT dividing by width, days / width otherwise WITHOUT snapWorkdays. Rounded UP, never down, so every quantised solution stays feasible in the real domain. Zero is legal: an explicit zero duration is a real plan state.

width.$comment: people. A whole number of people, at least one — refused at the domain boundary by schedule.ts:478 for the same reason it is bounded here: duration is effort divided by width, so a width of 0 is Infinity days and a fractional width is people that do not exist.

personId.$comment: null means unassigned, which is a real and common state (schedule.ts:42). The solver only ever asks 'the same person as that slice?', so the value is opaque.

poolIds.$comment: A SET, empty when the row names no sized team — the ordinary state of a plan with no team sizes, and it reserves nothing and waits for nothing. The whole width is spent in EVERY named pool for the whole duration (Dany, 2026-08-13, decision 3): three teams on a five-day block take five days in each of the three pools, not five days split between them. Emitted sorted so the canonical input hashes stably; sortedness is a builder invariant this schema cannot state.

priorityWeight.$comment: dimensionless. The DENSE RANK (R + 1) − rank(p(s)) over the R distinct resolved leaf priorities present in this canonical input, rank 1-based ascending; 0 when no priority reaches the leaf. Never the absolute authored priority: asOptionalPriority accepts any safe integer with no ceiling, so P_max + 1 loses precision at Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and Σ w(s)·finish(s) overflows CP-SAT's 64-bit linear expressions. Resolved by importing priorityByLeaf from libs/domain, never reimplemented — it is a nearest/most-specific OVERRIDE (first non-null walking leaf-upward), so leaf 5 under parent 1 resolves to 5, not 1.

notBeforeUnits.$comment: units from day zero. The latest of the leaf's own floor and every ancestor's, already folded.

deadlineUnits.$comment: units from day zero, or null for unconstrained. The EFFECTIVE deadline for this slice, already folded over the tree by the same leaf-upward walk and already converted to (D + 1) × quantum, so the solver applies it without seeing the tree exactly as it never sees reach. THAT MULTIPLE IS AN INVARIANT AND IT IS EXPRESSIBLE HERE, WHICH TASK-303 SAID IT WAS NOT. Its argument was that multipleOf takes a literal while the divisor is this request own quantum one object up, which JSON Schema cannot reference — both halves true, and the conclusion does not follow, because THIS FILE ALSO FIXES THE QUANTUM: quantum is const 48 one object up, so the literal and the reference are the same number by construction and 48 is that literal. The two must be edited together and the pair is the invariant, not either line. INDEPENDENT VALIDATION OF THIS INVARIANT EXISTS AND IS NOT THIS LINE (TASK-329 AC #1). Three guards state it apart from the schema: revalidateSolverResult refuses it while proving the REQUEST, above its non-feasible early return, so the rule reaches an infeasible or unknown answer; revalidateOptimizedDeadlines (TASK-303) still refuses it after materialising, because that is a separate entry point and a validator assuming its sibling already ran is not independent; and Python check_cross_field refuses it against this request own quantum rather than against the literal. What made the first of those reachable is the call-site half: evaluateSolverOutcome re-validates BEFORE it dispositions response status, where until TASK-329 it returned plan-infeasible first and a malformed request could acquire a sticky certificate. A schema is what the sender and receiver agreed to; the independent guards are for when the sender is wrong about that. Why it matters: a deadlineUnits that is not a multiple yields a FRACTIONAL due day that isOnTime was never written to take, and the CP-SAT model then admits a placement this side refuses as deadline-violated. Zero is legal and is the unmeetable deadline: due day -1, missed by every non-negative placement — and zero is a multiple of 48, so this constraint does not touch it.

workItemIsMilestone.$comment: True exactly when every slice sharing workItemKey has durationUnits 0. Such an item is a milestone and its deadline constraint gives it one solver unit of occupancy. False for every slice of an item containing positive work, including its zero-duration steps: those steps are endpoints inside the projected work-item span and do not extend an exactly-met deadline into the next workday. Both consumers independently group on workItemKey and SHALL NOT parse key to reconstruct it.

value.$comment: units. The term recomputed on the PUBLISHED offsets, and the only field Bun re-validates by recomputation. Not the stage incumbent: a later stage minimising T2 under T1 <= v1 may legitimately return a schedule whose T1 is strictly better than v1 (Sol r7 Critical 1).

stageValue.$comment: units. The incumbent that stage found; null when it found none.

bound.$comment: units. That stage's best dual bound; null when the stage produced none.

status.$comment: A statement about the STAGE, never about the published schedule. Exactly three values, fixed by design.md's stage-status matrix, which is the single authority this schema and the 4.8 validator are generated from. NOT THE SAME THREE VALUES AS #/$defs/response's status, and not the same question: this one is PROOF STRENGTH and admits 'optimal'; that one is the RUN OUTCOME and refuses 'optimal' precisely because a response-level one would claim the published schedule is optimal. The two sets overlap on 'feasible' and 'unknown' and must never be merged or cross-validated — a codec that reuses one validator for both would silently admit a response status of 'optimal'. 'quantisation-floor' is a publication tag and is NEVER a status here (Sol r8 Critical 5, kimi r8 Important 2). Bun additionally checks value <= stageValue when both are present; that relation is not expressible in JSON Schema.

objectiveValues.$comment: All three terms are always present; a stage that never ran reports status 'unknown' with null stageValue and bound rather than omitting its term. TERM KEYS ARE LOWERCASE, derived rather than invented: tasks.md 4.12b spells the stored shape Record<'makespan'|'priority'|'movement', ObjectiveValue>, and it is the only artifact that writes the keys at all. MAKESPAN, PRIORITY and MOVEMENT in design.md are the mathematical term NAMES, not JSON keys. FALSIFIER: any artifact that pins a different wire spelling, or a codec step that case-converts between wire and stored — either would mean this file chose wrong and a translation nobody specified exists.

contractVersion.$comment: "<SCHEDULER_CONTRACT_VERSION>+<solverVersion>". solverVersion alone was unsound: durations, the leaf expansion and baselineOffsets are produced by Bun/domain code the Python package version does not describe.

objective.$comment: pri minimises (PRIORITY, MAKESPAN, MOVEMENT) lexicographically; time minimises (MAKESPAN, PRIORITY, MOVEMENT). Neither is a total order — ties exist and production is not required to break them reproducibly.

budgetMs.$comment: milliseconds of wall clock for the whole staged run.

stageBudgetSplit.$comment: Dimensionless fractions of budgetMs, one per stage. STAGE_BUDGET_SPLIT = [0.60, 0.25, 0.15], an exported constant; a stage that finishes early donates its remainder to the next. That the three sum to 1 is a builder invariant, not expressible here.

quantum.$comment: units per workday, and PINNED rather than merely documented. SOLVER_QUANTUM = 48 is covered by SCHEDULER_CONTRACT_VERSION, so this wire generation has exactly one legal quantum and saying so is what lets deadlineUnits carry its multipleOf as a literal. Before TASK-329 this read `type: integer, minimum: 1` while the guard divided by the constant, so {quantum: 24, deadlineUnits: 24} was wire-valid and request-relative-valid yet refused, and {quantum: 50, deadlineUnits: 96} passed the guard while violating the invariant the comment claimed. build-solver-request.ts emits SOLVER_QUANTUM unconditionally, so nothing production has ever sent becomes invalid here. A future quantum ships solver-wire.v2.json beside this file, exactly as wireVersion says a generation does, rather than widening this const.

horizonUnits.$comment: units. The SERIAL bound max(0, ...notBeforeUnits) + Σ durationUnits — seeded with zero because a plan with slices and no manual floors is the default state of nearly every project and an unseeded max over an empty set has no value (schedule.ts:2051 writes Math.max(0, ...) for the same shape). Not the Fast makespan plus remaining effort, which stops being an upper bound once the optimizer may idle a slice. NOT tightened to the latest deadline: that would make an infeasible plan indistinguishable from a horizon overflow. Bounded by 2^31 − 1 here because the builder fails with horizon-overflow above it before spawning (2.10), so an over-horizon request is a builder bug that never reaches a process.

slices.$comment: A canonical input with zero slices, or one whose durations are all zero, allocates no slot and spawns nothing, so an empty array never reaches the wire.

pools.$comment: How many slots each pool holds, keyed by pool id — the wire form of the canonical PoolSizes = ReadonlyMap<string, number> (schedule.ts:95), which is why it is a map. Size is an integer of at least 1: project_team_capacity.size is `integer('size').notNull()` with the floor enforced at be-01's boundary (repository/schema.ts), and the floor is a correctness bound rather than a preference — a pool of 0 slots is a plan of Infinity dates. An UNSTATED pool is absent rather than present as null or zero, exactly as it is absent from slotsOf: unstated constrains nothing. A pool nothing references may be absent entirely; a pool some slice names may NOT be, and that is the invariant below.

baselineOffsets.$comment: units. The QUANTISED Fast baseline — Fast's own placement re-run through the same schedule() code path over the rounded integer durationUnits — and the only movement reference either objective uses. NOT real Fast's offsets, whose fractional days/width starts can be infeasible in the integer model on legal widths: three serial slices with days=1, width=5 put real Fast at 28.8 units where the rounded model needs 30, so real Fast's value is not a satisfiable upper bound. MOVEMENT is measured against these, so it always has an integer representation.

fastHint.$comment: units. The CP-SAT solution hint, and it is the SAME VALUE as baselineOffsets — both are the quantised Fast baseline produced by one re-run (design.md 'The bound and the hint come from the quantised baseline'; tasks.md 2.11). Two fields because the roles differ: this one seeds the search, baselineOffsets defines MOVEMENT and stage 1's upper bound. Their equality is a builder invariant this schema cannot state; see the request's own $comment.

request.$comment: CROSS-FIELD INVARIANTS JSON SCHEMA CANNOT EXPRESS. Each is enforced by the Bun request builder before spawn AND re-checked by the Python entrypoint after validation, and each carries a watched red in the contract suite: (1) fastHint and baselineOffsets are equal as maps — perturb one fastHint entry by one unit and the contract test must fail; a wire that carries two copies of one value invites exactly that divergence. (2) The key sets of slices[].key, baselineOffsets and fastHint are equal — no extra key, no missing key. (3) Every offset in baselineOffsets and fastHint is <= horizonUnits. (4) Every poolId named by any slice has an entry in pools — this is schedule.ts:718's `no size for pool ${poolId}` throw promoted to the wire, and a default here would be a capacity constraint silently not applied; drop one entry and the builder must refuse pre-spawn rather than let the solver place the slice unconstrained. (5) Every edge endpoint is a key in slices. (6) stageBudgetSplit sums to 1. (7) No duplicate key in any object-shaped map, checked against the raw member count, because both JSON.parse and json.loads silently keep the last. (8) The exact worst cases Σ w(s) × (horizonUnits + durationUnits(s)) for PRIORITY and Σ |offset − baseline| for MOVEMENT are <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, accumulated in bigint and compared against BigInt(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) before conversion, failing with objective-overflow. PRIORITY'S WORST CASE IS OVER FINISHES, NOT OVER THE HORIZON: horizonUnits bounds a slice's START (offset-domain) and a finish past it is legal, so Σ w(s) × horizonUnits is short by exactly Σ w(s) × durationUnits(s). Measured, not reasoned — at horizonUnits 2^31 − 1 and priorityWeight 2^22 the horizon-only bound is 9007199250546688 and accepts the request, while CP-SAT proves OPTIMAL a placement publishing priority.value 9007199254740992, one unit past this schema's own safeInteger, so the response would be refused by the consumer that asked for it. BOTH ARMS CARRY IT, and they differ in where the horizon comes from: the Bun builder checks it before spawn against the horizon it DERIVES from the slices, while validate.py's check_cross_field re-derives it after schema validation from the horizonUnits ON THE WIRE (alongside 2, 3, 5 and 7), so a request reaching the CLI by any route other than that builder is refused with exit 64 rather than solved into a response the asking consumer would have to reject. The Python arm needs no bigint - its integers are arbitrary precision - so it compares against the literal 9007199254740991, which is this schema's bound rather than the language's. MOVEMENT's arm cannot fire at today's ceiling in either language: invariant 3 bounds every term by horizonUnits and this schema caps that at 2^31 - 1, so the sum needs over four million slices to reach the ceiling; it is carried in both arms so that raising the horizon cannot leave one lagging the other.

status.$comment: A RUN-OUTCOME vocabulary, and a DIFFERENT question from #/$defs/objective-term's status: that one reports how strong a stage's proof is, this one reports WHETHER A SCHEDULE IS BEING RETURNED AT ALL and, if not, which of the two reasons applies. Exactly three values, and every one of them was read out of an artifact rather than chosen for how it reads. `infeasible` — spec.md 'The response `status` SHALL admit `infeasible` as a first-class outcome' pins the token verbatim; it is a PROOF that the submitted constraint system has no solution and never becomes feasible with more budget. `unknown` — pinned by the same sentence's second half, 'and it SHALL NOT be mapped onto `unknown`', which is only meaningful if `unknown` is itself a response status; it is budget exhausted with no incumbent and no proof, and it is the matrix's `UNKNOWN, no incumbent, k = 1` row. `feasible` — the only other outcome any matrix row produces: every publishing row publishes an incumbent, an incumbent is by construction feasible for the original constraints, and nothing more than that is ever claimed for it. `optimal` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and by an artifact rather than by taste: design.md's four-fields paragraph says the per-stage 'optimal' 'never claims the published schedule is optimal, WHICH THE DESIGN HAS SAID FROM THE START IT IS NOT'. A response-level 'optimal' would make exactly that claim, so candidate (a) — reusing the stage vocabulary plus infeasible — is refused by the same design that owns the matrix. Proof strength is already carried per term; this field must not report it a second time and less precisely.

offsets.$comment: units from day zero, one per slice, same units as notBeforeUnits and horizonUnits. Bun divides by quantum before materialising, so what is stored is in the fractional workday unit Fast already uses. Bun independently re-validates every offset — non-negative, an integer multiple of one unit, within horizonUnits — plus every edge, floor, pool capacity, assignee non-overlap and effective deadline, and recomputes every objectiveValues[T].value, before anything is stored. These offsets are an intermediate and are never persisted alone.

allOf.$comment: THE status/offsets CONDITIONAL, taken from the matrix's own `n/a` rather than invented. `feasible` is the only status that publishes, so it is the only one that carries offsets and objectiveValues, and it carries BOTH. `unknown` and `infeasible` carry NEITHER, because the matrix writes `n/a` in the objectiveValues column for all three of its stopping rows and `value` is BY DEFINITION 'the term recomputed on the published offsets' — with nothing published, all three `value` fields have no referent and a required non-negative integer would have to be a lie or a sentinel. offsets is ABSENT rather than `{}`: an empty map is a well-formed offsetMap, so it would pass the schema and then fail request invariant (2) key-set equality one layer later, reporting a vocabulary decision as a corrupt payload.

response.$comment: The response carries at most these four members and never any other. The lifecycle wrapper's childDeadlineAt and attemptToken are process arguments rather than message fields, so neither enters this schema, the golden corpus, or the solved model. Two of the four are conditional on `status` — see the allOf below — which is why `required` names only wireVersion and status; spec.md's 'SHALL carry only { wireVersion, status, offsets, objectiveValues }' is a closed maximum, not a floor. A LATER-STAGE INFEASIBLE HAS NO ENCODING HERE, ON PURPOSE. design.md's `INFEASIBLE, k > 1` row argues that every constraint a later stage adds is already satisfied by the previous incumbent, so such a result 'cannot become infeasible unless the model is wrong', and it SHALL NOT be reported as plan-infeasible. `infeasible` on this wire therefore means one thing only — a proof about the submitted constraint system — and a solver that hits INFEASIBLE at k > 1 holds, in memory, a counterexample to its own solver's answer. It SHALL exit non-zero WITHOUT emitting a response rather than emit a proof it can itself refute; the coordinator records that run as `invalid-output`, which is the disposition the matrix already assigns that row. THE CODE IS `70` AND ONLY THAT OUTCOME TAKES IT (TASK-310): a CP-SAT MODEL_INVALID also emits no response, but it is not a row of that matrix and exits `71` for `internal-error`, so this sentence describes one branch of the entrypoint rather than every silent exit. FALSIFIER for this whole decision: an artifact that requires the coordinator to tell 'the solver crashed' from 'the solver contradicted itself' FROM THE RESPONSE — that would need a fourth status and this file chose wrong.
